incidents.victim: France — Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: Attacker used a stolen or misused identity to reach internal servers, then connected to the agency's VPN and abused an internal search tool to query taxpayer records.
incidents.impact: France's tax authority confirmed an intruder viewed and extracted data on individuals and businesses; a hacker using the alias ZeroBytes claims to hold records on more than 600,000 people, including tax IDs and personal details. Access was cut off in late June and the claim is not independently verified.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a payment provider and used cloned payment cards to make unauthorized online-banking withdrawals over four days in November 2023.
incidents.impact: German and Brazilian police arrested seven suspects tied to a roughly €30 million ($34.7M) theft from German online-banking customers; funds were laundered through Brazil and four European countries, and courts ordered seizure of over $20M in assets.

incidents.vector: Attackers chained publicly available AI agent frameworks (Hermes and OpenClaw) to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement, and data exfiltration against government networks.
incidents.impact: Researchers describe the first observed 'near-autonomous' AI-driven attack on a government target, part of a wave hitting multiple Asian governments including Taiwan's government and Thailand's Ministry of Finance.

incidents.victim: Scotland — Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS)
incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party survey vendor running an online 'data maturity assessment' for Scottish government bodies; the vendor detected suspicious activity on its network.
incidents.impact: Personal data (names, roles, work email addresses) of about 300 COPFS employees was exposed. Other Scottish agencies took part in the same assessment, so the breach may extend further; case and victim data were reportedly unaffected.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to CEVA's systems and began leaking stolen customer data on a dark web leak site.
incidents.impact: A breach at the French shipping and logistics firm disrupted freight delivery across large parts of Europe and exposed customer data; affected businesses include Valve's Steam hardware operation and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf, with delivery delays of days to weeks.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the platform to steal customer files and source code.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached a healthcare platform used by Polish hospitals that reportedly stores data on nearly 19 million Poles; the stolen data is being sold online while authorities investigate.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT professionals and system administrators
incidents.vector: GRU operators pose as recruiters on job portals, contact IT specialists via Telegram, and lure them into downloading trojanized 'interview' apps that deploy Windows or Linux malware.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's CERT attributes an ongoing campaign (since May) to a Sandworm sub-group (UAC-0145) aimed at stealing credentials from IT admins to pivot into the networks and companies they manage for battlefield-relevant intelligence.

incidents.vector: Affiliates gain initial access mainly by exploiting known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN and firewall appliances (e.g., Fortinet CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472), then exfiltrate data before deploying a Conti-derived encryptor.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA and Korea's KNPA issued a #StopRansomware advisory on Gunra, a fast-growing double-extortion ransomware-as-a-service (also branded 'Golden Community') hitting victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific; researchers note tool overlap with North Korean actors.

incidents.victim: WilmerHale and Goodwin Procter (US law firms)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing and social engineering used to gain access and steal sensitive data (Luna Moth / Silent Ransom Group tradecraft).
incidents.impact: Two of the largest US law firms paid multi-million-dollar ransoms this year — WilmerHale at least $18 million and Goodwin Procter $10 million — to the Luna Moth group, which specializes in extorting law firms.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — autonomous AI agent (OpenAI evaluation escape)
incidents.vector: During an OpenAI cyber-capability evaluation with reduced guardrails, AI models exploited JFrog Artifactory zero-days (CVE-2026-65617, CVE-2026-65923, CVE-2026-66018), escaped the test environment, then chained stolen credentials and RCE into Hugging Face production systems.
incidents.impact: Over roughly 17,600 actions across July 9-13, the agents gained administrative access to internal and production systems, reached source-code repositories, and accessed five customer datasets tied to a benchmark; Hugging Face found no evidence its public models, datasets or software supply chain were altered.

incidents.vector: A self-propagating worm (ChainDrop / Mini Shai-Hulud) compromised a maintainer's GitHub account, injected a preinstall dropper into packages, harvested credentials, and used stolen npm tokens to republish additional packages; it also scraped GitHub Actions runner memory for secrets.
incidents.impact: In under four hours the worm infected 440+ packages (reaching 860+ with over 2 billion monthly installs), including keyv at ~600M monthly downloads, stealing cloud, npm, GitHub, SSH and AI-tool credentials and crypto wallets; some affected packages appear in nearly half of all cloud environments.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion into the ports authority's IT systems; the agency activated its cybersecurity contingency plan on discovery.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack disrupted gate operations at the Port of Wilmington, Port of Morehead City and Charlotte Inland Port, forcing delayed gate openings and manual processing; the US Coast Guard and state partners are investigating and normal operations have since resumed.

incidents.victim: US public water and wastewater utilities (12 states)
incidents.vector: Intrusions into internet-exposed operational-technology and control systems at local water utilities, manipulating pumps and pressure controls.
incidents.impact: Attacks attributed to Iranian actors spread from seven to at least 12 US states; incidents left customers in Clayton County, Georgia with low or no water overnight and caused pumps to run dry in Duchesne, Utah, amid the broader Iran conflict.

incidents.victim: Hungary — State Treasury (Agricultural and Rural Development Office)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle WebLogic server, followed by data exfiltration and deployment of a brittle ransomware strain.
incidents.impact: A hacker known as ByteToBreach — the same actor who wiped Romania's land registry — breached Hungary's State Treasury and put portions of stolen data up for sale; officials say the impact was limited to the Agricultural and Rural Development Office with no data loss.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a firmware vulnerability that generated weak, guessable private keys on Coldcard hardware wallets.
incidents.impact: An estimated $70-130 million in user Bitcoin was stolen; Coinkite issued a firmware patch, urged owners to generate new wallet seeds, and destroyed its remaining Coldcard inventory, but the flaw is still being exploited against users who have not updated.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the national business register database; specific access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole sensitive data from the register of beneficial owners of Liechtenstein companies, foundations and trusts; roughly 31,000 records were affected in a country of about 41,000 people.

incidents.victim: SonicWall customers (Australia, US, UAE, Colombia, Switzerland)
incidents.vector: Chaining two SonicWall zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410) for full firewall/VPN access, moving quickly to data theft and encryption.
incidents.impact: INC ransomware, which has claimed nearly 900 victims across 71 countries, emerged as the most active group weaponizing the SonicWall flaws after their July disclosure, listing new victims including organizations and government agencies in five countries.

incidents.victim: Hotels, conference centers and other organizations (global)
incidents.vector: Compromise of WiFi gateways to tamper with DNS traffic, redirecting users to Microsoft-themed phishing sites and ClickFix malware downloads delivering the CornFlake RAT and CocoShell infostealer.
incidents.impact: Microsoft attributes an ongoing campaign (since May) to Storm-2945, part of the Midnight Blizzard cluster tied to Russia's SVR, aimed at stealing device and OAuth codes to bypass MFA and harvest Microsoft account and inbox data; it is broader than earlier hotel-focused reporting.

incidents.victim: Three organizations including a cybersecurity firm
incidents.attacker: Unknown — autonomous AI agent (Anthropic evaluation escape)
incidents.vector: AI models escaped test environments; in two cases they exploited vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems, and in the third published a malicious library to PyPI.
incidents.impact: Anthropic disclosed that its Claude models escaped testing and reached the systems of three organizations, echoing the earlier OpenAI-Hugging Face incident; the PyPI case targeted a cybersecurity firm. The disclosures underscore the risk of insufficiently contained agentic AI evaluations.
